screen19-a1.glyph: three horizontal lines of decreasing length
screen19-a1.description: three stacked lines control in the top-left corner of the toolbar
screen19-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Open menu" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a1.convention_relied_on: three stacked horizontal lines (hamburger) is an established convention for opening the app's navigation menu — my reading, confidence high
screen19-a1.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but the hamburger glyph is a widely-known convention; common-icon exemption applies pending the behavioural test
screen19-a1.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a1 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: tapping the hamburger opened the side navigation panel, exactly what the convention promises

screen19-a2.glyph: ghost outline with two dots for eyes
screen19-a2.description: ghost outline glyph in the top-right corner of the toolbar
screen19-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Incognito chat" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a2.convention_relied_on: a ghost outline is not an established mobile convention; I know of no common meaning a first-time user could rely on — my reading, confidence high that it is not a convention
screen19-a2.initial_rationale: no visible text anywhere near it and the ghost is not a recognizable convention; nothing on the screen says what it does
screen19-a2.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a2 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: no label, tooltip or adjacent copy exists before the tap, and the ghost glyph is not a convention; the explanation is shown only after the user has already switched modes
screen19-a2.recommendation: put a visible word beside or under the glyph, e.g. 'Incognito' (or 'Private chat'), so the mode is named before it is switched on

screen19-a3.description: 'Upgrade to Pro' link at the right of the grey banner above the typing box
screen19-a3.visible_text: "Upgrade to Pro" beside the banner text "Get more with Claude Pro"
screen19-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Upgrade to Pro" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a3.initial_rationale: explicit verb and object; a first-time user can tell it leads to upgrading to a paid Pro plan
screen19-a3.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a3 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the link opened the plan screen it names

screen19-a4.description: text entry box at the bottom of the screen
screen19-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Chat with Claude…" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a4.initial_rationale: placeholder names what goes in (a chat message to Claude); no format or constraint matters for free text
screen19-a4.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a4 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the placeholder survives focus and names the job; it is replaced only by the user's own message, with a send arrow appearing

screen19-a5.glyph: plus sign in a grey circle
screen19-a5.description: plus sign in a grey circle at the left of the typing bar
screen19-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Add to chat" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a5.convention_relied_on: a plus in a message composer is an established 'add/attach' convention — my reading, confidence high
screen19-a5.initial_rationale: unlabeled plus in the composer toolbar; add/attach convention; exemption pending the behavioural test
screen19-a5.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a5 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the plus opened the 'Add to chat' sheet, as the add convention promises

screen19-a6.description: pill in the typing bar with the words 'Haiku 4.5'
screen19-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Haiku 4.5" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a6.initial_rationale: the pill shows a proper name and a version number; nothing says it is a model, or that pressing it lets you change which one answers — a first-time user has no way to read 'Haiku 4.5' as a setting
screen19-a6.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a6 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the purpose ('choose the model') is disclosed only by the sheet the tap opens; the pill's face is a product name a first-time user cannot interpret
screen19-a6.recommendation: show the purpose on the pill, e.g. 'Model: Haiku 4.5 ▾', or a caption 'Choose model'

screen19-a7.glyph: microphone outline in a grey circle
screen19-a7.description: microphone outline in a grey circle, second from the right in the typing bar
screen19-a7.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Start speech input" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a7.convention_relied_on: a microphone is an established 'speak / dictate' convention — my reading, confidence high
screen19-a7.initial_rationale: unlabeled microphone in a text composer; dictation convention; exemption pending the behavioural test
screen19-a7.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a7 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the microphone opened a voice-dictation intro, matching the convention

screen19-a8.glyph: white vertical bars of varying height in a black circle
screen19-a8.description: round black button with white vertical bars at the right end of the typing bar
screen19-a8.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Voice Mode" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen19-a8.convention_relied_on: vertical bars of varying height suggest sound in general, but this is not an established control convention a first-time user could map to one action; sitting beside a microphone it does not distinguish itself — my reading, confidence medium
screen19-a8.initial_rationale: no visible text, and the sound-bars glyph is not a recognizable convention; next to a microphone nothing says how it differs
screen19-a8.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a8 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: verification found no visible text in any reachable state and the glyph is not a convention; the behavioural tap could not be run, so the verdict is provisional
screen19-a8.recommendation: add a visible label such as 'Talk' or 'Voice chat' under or beside the button, distinct from the microphone
